summary: Irreversible DROP COLUMN plus a non-idempotent, untransacted delete; the guarded CREATE statements are decoys.

must_not_find.why: Both CREATE statements already use IF NOT EXISTS and are safe to re-run. Flagging them as non-idempotent means the reviewer did not read the guard it is complaining about the absence of. This is the entry that failed the gate on 2026-08-05 and 2026-09-18: the whole migration is an added file, so every keyword here was a quote of it, and an evidence block that reached up from the DELETE to the CREATE statements scored the right answer as a decoy hit. Each keyword now demands the guard that is already there. None is the bare word 'idempotent' — the real defect IS non-idempotent and must_find matches on 'idempoten', so that word cannot separate the two claims; only the demand for IF NOT EXISTS can.
